Separate what is known from what is assumed. Every sentence in "facts" and "why_mispriced" must cite pack ids like
[f:…], [m:…], [s:…], [c:…], and every number must match the pack exactly. Put your reasoning in "inferences"
(each starting with "Inference:") and the things that must hold for the thesis in "assumptions" (each starting
with "Assumption:"; mark any number you choose with "(assumed)"). Kill criteria must be observable: a metric id from
the pack, an operator, a threshold, and a check-after date after the next filing window. Write plainly. No hype,
no certainty words, no price targets.

assumptions: Assumption: the $600,000,000 order [f:6f1c2a52-3b1e-4c43-9e59-3d1b1f0a0002] converts to revenue inside the RPO duration and is not practically cancellable.

Assumption: fiscal 2027 capex of $1,800,000,000 [f:6f1c2a52-3b1e-4c43-9e59-3d1b1f0a0001] is funded without equity issuance that lifts diluted shares materially above 212,000,000 [m:diluted_shares:2026-06-30].
Assumption: operating margin holds near 0.1650 [m:op_margin_ttm] through the capex build, i.e. depreciation and mix do not compress it by more than (assumed) 3 points.
Assumption: receivables growth, once disclosed, does not run materially faster than revenue growth; this is the check that R2 could not run [s:R2].
Assumption: fiscal 2027 capex is a peak year rather than a new baseline; if it resets the run-rate, the cash story changes for longer than one year (assumed).

facts.text: Revenue was $980,000,000 in the year ended 2025-06-30 and $1,250,000,000 in the year ended 2026-06-30.
Operating income was $206,250,000 on $1,250,000,000 of revenue in the year ended 2026-06-30.
Remaining performance obligations were $2,900,000,000 at 2025-06-30 and $4,200,000,000 at 2026-06-30.
On 2026-08-06 the company guided fiscal 2027 capital expenditures to approximately $1,800,000,000.
The same 2026-08-06 release disclosed a $600,000,000 multi-year order from a hyperscale cloud provider.
The pack links that hyperscale cloud provider to the company as a customer, and the only capex category recorded is compute.
Signal S1 fired with strength 0.82 on inputs g_ob 0.4483, g_rev 0.2755, gap 0.1728 and consecutive 2.

inferences: Inference: order-book growth of 0.4483 [m:rpo_yoy] is running well ahead of fiscal-year revenue growth of 0.2755 [s:S1], so backlog is leading revenue rather than trailing it.

Inference: the $600,000,000 order [f:6f1c2a52-3b1e-4c43-9e59-3d1b1f0a0002] is a minority of the $4,200,000,000 RPO at 2026-06-30 [m:rpo:2026-06-30]; it supports the backlog step-up but does not account for it, so other awards are doing work the pack does not name.

Inference: guided fiscal 2027 capex of $1,800,000,000 [f:6f1c2a52-3b1e-4c43-9e59-3d1b1f0a0001] exceeds fiscal 2026 revenue of $1,250,000,000 [m:revenue:2026-06-30] and is roughly nine times operating income of $206,250,000 [m:op_income:2026-06-30]; the pack carries no cash, debt, or depreciation line, so the funding path is unverified.
Inference: R2 could not run because receivables_growth is missing [s:R2], so a 0.2755 revenue year [s:S1] is not yet confirmed as cash-collected growth.
Inference: S1 firing for 2 consecutive periods with a gap of 0.1728 [s:S1] reads as a persistent order-book lead, not a single-quarter artifact, but two periods is a short base for that claim.

kill_criteria.why: Backlog growth below 0.20 breaks the order-leads-revenue premise; 0.20 is a chosen threshold, not a pack value.
Margin below 0.12 during a capex year means the build is being absorbed through the P&L faster than the thesis allows; 0.12 is a chosen threshold.
TTM revenue growth below 0.10 would show the backlog is not converting; 0.10 is a chosen threshold.
Evidence score below 50 means the pack's own support has weakened; 50 is a chosen threshold.

risks.text: Capex of $1,800,000,000 against revenue of $1,250,000,000 is the central risk; the pack gives no funding source.
Revenue quality is unchecked because receivables_growth is missing and R2 status is unknown.
Customer concentration is unnamed in the pack; the counterparty is described only as a hyperscale cloud provider.

content.summary: Nimbus Compute Corp. (NMBS) grew fiscal 2026 revenue to $1,250,000,000 from $980,000,000 and RPO to $4,200,000,000 from $2,900,000,000, with a $600,000,000 hyperscaler order and fiscal 2027 capex guided to $1,800,000,000. The order book leads revenue; the capex bill is larger than revenue and its funding is not in the pack.

why_mispriced.text: The pack records a context gap of 58.3 and a C2 value of 0.06 built from g_implied 0.12 against g_evidence 0.18, which reads as growth evidence sitting above the growth embedded in the valuation inputs.
Backlog growth of 0.4483 against revenue growth of 0.2755 is the specific gap the pack is pointing at.

The $1,800,000,000 capex guide is a visible, dated cost that can be discounted now, while the $600,000,000 order and the RPO step-up convert over multiple years; that timing asymmetry is a plausible source of the discount.
Evidence at 62.5 against a gap of 58.3 says the pack sees a real but only moderately supported discrepancy, not a wide one.
